chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to a man: 'You and your wealth are for your father.' Then Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'And I do not like for him to take from the wealth of his son except what he is in need of, from what is necessary. Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, does not love corruption/mischief.'
ai.seo_question: What are the financial rights of a father over his son's wealth in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded in al-Kafi, clarifies the juristic debate regarding the father's right to his son's wealth by distinguishing between absolute ownership and usufruct for necessity. Imam al-Baqir (AS) refines the Prophet's statement that 'you and your wealth belong to your father' by limiting the father's extraction to essential needs, thereby preventing financial mismanagement. This principle aligns with the Shia legal concept that while the father has priority, he must act as a prudent steward rather than a consumer of the son's capital.

en.hubeali:
Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Hamza Al Sumaly, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said to a man: ‘You and your wealth is for your father’. Then Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And I<sup>asws</sup> do not like it for him that he should take from the wealth of his son except what he is needy to it, from what is a must from it. Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty does not Love the mischief’.
en.sarwar: 3. Sahl ibn Ziyad has narrated from ibn Mahbub from abu Hamzah al-Thumaliy who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, once said to a man, ‘You and your property belong to your father.’

Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, then said, ‘I do not like his spending from the property of his son more than what he needs for his bare necessities; Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, does not love destruction.’”
